title: Feature creep - Let's make the drivers have emotions
author: johnesco
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/frkvyvbnrcrh1.png?width=315&format=png&auto=webp&s=09fdce4627b9d939c08ce93872eefa27eafa517c

I've put a lot of work in the car physics of my game. I've decided that what I also want is a "mood engine" for having the other drivers react to the player. (not sure how much if any will show textually in the final, this is my debug view)  


I may decide to make it a toggle, would this be info you'd want to know, or just focus on racing?

comments.author: DepartmentPlus5191
comments.body: I really like this idea! Having the other drivers react to you could make it feel like a multiplayer game even when you're racing solo. I'd definitely want to see it, and a toggle sounds like a great way to let people choose.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body:
It's currently online at https://vibecodedgames.itch.io/pavement

Without the mood engine and when I publish a draft of it I'll let you know when it's live. Some interesting things I'm working out is should arrival stay mad between races and how long till it fades or have you made an enemy for the rest of the game?

replies.author: DepartmentPlus5191
replies.body:
Thanks for sharing the link, I'll check it out!

For the rival's emotions, it might help to look at how real drivers react on the road. I live in Korea, where a lot of people are packed into small areas, so cars often end up bunched together like in your game. From what I've seen, when someone drives aggressively, people get angry really quickly, but they also forget about it just as fast once the other car is out of sight. Maybe a quick-to-anger, quick-to-fade mood could feel pretty natural for most drivers, while a few rivals could hold a grudge longer to make things interesting.
